title: Algebraic field-valued images over closed base points are closed in decent spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume that every point of $|X|$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism from the spectrum of a field. Here monomorphism means injectivity of composition on morphisms from every algebraic space over $S$; quasi-compact means that after every scheme test inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ an $S$-morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $s\in S$ be the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}L$. If $\{s\}$ is closed and the induced field extension $\kappa(s)\to L$ is algebraic (each element of $L$ satisfies a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $\kappa(s)$), then the image of $a$ is a closed singleton in $|X|$. The residue field $\kappa(s)$ and its induced map are [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 07U5 (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point); the hypothesis on field monomorphisms is decency by Tag 03JV (lemma-UR-finite-above-x), condition (4), and Definition 03I8 (definition-very-reasonable).

proof.text: Write $x$ for the image of $a$. Let $x_0\in\overline{\{x\}}$ be arbitrary. The atlas in [def-trf-algebraic-space] supplies a representable surjective etale $p:U\to X$ and $u_0\in U$ over $x_0$. The field-monomorphism hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-decent-space-etale-generalization-lifting]; apply it to $x\leadsto x_0$ to obtain $u\leadsto u_0$ with $p(u)=x$.

Form $W=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_XU$. It is a scheme and $q:W\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is etale by the scheme-test definition of representable etaleness of $p$. The unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $u$ have common image $x$. Thus [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] gives $w\in W$ mapping to $u$. For this etale scheme morphism $q$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] says that the residue extension $L\to\kappa(w)$ is finite separable, in particular each of its elements satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $L$.

The maps of schemes $W\to U\to S$ induce field inclusions $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)\to\kappa(w)$, compatible with $\kappa(s)\to L\to\kappa(w)$ by commutativity of the fibre-product diagram and the definition of residue-field maps. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-element-tower] to the latter tower: every element of $\kappa(w)$ is algebraic over $\kappa(s)$. For $c\in\kappa(u)$ take a nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(s)$ annihilating its image in $\kappa(w)$. Injectivity of $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(w)$ implies that the same polynomial vanishes at $c$. Thus $\kappa(u)/\kappa(s)$ is algebraic.

The point $u$ maps to $s$ under $U\to S$, and $s$ is closed by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-algebraic-residue-closed-point] to conclude that $\{u\}$ is closed in $U$. Since $u\leadsto u_0$, we have $u=u_0$, hence $x=p(u)=p(u_0)=x_0$. Every point of $\overline{\{x\}}$ is therefore $x$, so this closure is $\{x\}$. The image of $a$, whose source has one point, is this closed singleton.

lean.statement: theorem isClosed_pointImage_of_algebraic_residueField {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hdecent : ∀ x : Point X.obj.obj, ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ S) (i : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), schemePointMap i (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x ∧ (∀ (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (f g : Y.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk b)), f ≫ i = g ≫ i → f = g) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ QuasiCompact p.left) i) (L : Type u) [Field L] (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of L) ⟶ S) (a : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj) (hs : IsClosed ({b (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)} : Set S)) (halg : ∀ c : L, ∃ p : Polynomial (S.residueField (b (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L))), p ≠ 0 ∧ p.eval₂ (S.descResidueField (Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo b)).hom c = 0) : IsClosed ({schemePointMap a (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)} : Set (Point X.obj.obj)) ∧ pointImage a = {schemePointMap a (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)}
